text:
sara: heads-up: restores from staging snapshot s-2026-03-22-17 came back OK but we have no KMS grant logged for the decrypt step. noticed while auditing retention restores.

mike: hmm — do we have the S3/object metadata or uploader logs? could be sse-c vs cmk mismatch.

sara: pasted metadata from the object: `x-amz-meta-encrypt: sse-c` but the snapshot manifest shows `encryption: CMK` earlier. metadata and manifest disagree. also the restore event in restore-service shows `restore:success` but `kms:GrantUsed` is absent in audit logs.

backup-bot: snapshot-uploader v2.3.1 finished multipart upload for snapshot s-2026-03-22-17 parts=6 uploader_sa=svc-backup-staging

leo: I pushed gateway change yesterday that rewrites multipart headers to strip customer-provided encryption headers during chunking if backend=legacy. possibly the header got dropped on multipart assemble. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingest/merge/6789 (revert candidate).

anita: if headers were stripped the uploader SA may not have gotten a CMK grant call, so audit logs won't show KMS activity. confirm whether uploader made `GenerateDataKey` / `Encrypt`/`Grant` calls. can someone run `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=s-2026-03-22-17` for the timeframe?

mike: good call. also check KMS `list-grants --key-id alias/backup-staging` for recent grants and `aws logs filter-log-events` on kms proxy. if grants don't exist, we need to treat these snapshots as "unencrypted at rest" until proven otherwise. quarantine recommended.

sara: agreed. proposed short runbook: 1) mark snapshot quarantined in catalog 2) block restore API for snapshot id 3) run CloudTrail + kms grant checks 4) if uploader broke, rollback gateway change and re-upload snapshot with correct CMK metadata 5) notify compliance and affected teams.

leo: ok I can revert the gateway patch and kick a re-upload job: `./scripts/revert-gateway 6789 && ./scripts/reprocess-snapshot s-2026-03-22-17` — will do in ~15m.

anita: also add an alert rule: if restore-success event occurs without matching `kms:Encrypt`/`kms:Decrypt` audit events within +-30s, trigger PagerDuty. this would catch missing-grant cases going forward. can we add a lightweight SIEM matcher?

mike: +1 for alert. add a temporary detection that scans for `restore-service` logs with `restore:success` and joins to CloudTrail for KMS events. put it as a 24h-rate limit rule so we don't spam.

sara: assigning follow-ups: leo = revert + reprocess, mike = detection rule, anita = compliance notification + audit notes. I'll update the incident board. thanks all :thumbsup:

leo: ack. posting revert PR now -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingest/pull/459 (wip).

mike: once reverted I'll run a small smoke reupload on a staging snapshot and validate `aws cloudtrail` shows `GenerateDataKey` calls.

anita: also: we should check RBAC on uploader SA to ensure it didn't temporarily lose kms:Encrypt permission during the deploy (role rotate?). kube events show a short rollout at 16:58 — correlate.

sara: good point. i'll pull the role-change audit and paste here in 10m. going to create a short postmortem note after we confirm.
